task:
Intersection checks report true for comparators that can never match. No version is below 0.0.0, yet new Comparator('<0.0.0').intersects(new Comparator('<0.1.0')) returns true.

Without includePrerelease, both '<0.0.0' and '<0.0.0-0' match nothing. Each of these must return false, in both orders:

- new Comparator('<0.0.0').intersects(new Comparator('<0.1.0'), { includePrerelease: undefined })
- new Comparator('<0.0.0-0').intersects(new Comparator('<0.1.0'), { includePrerelease: undefined })

With { includePrerelease: true }, '<0.0.0-0' still matches nothing, so new Comparator('<0.0.0-0').intersects(new Comparator('<0.1.0'), { includePrerelease: true }) must be false in both orders. In that mode '<0.0.0' is not empty, because 0.0.0-1 is below it, so it still intersects '<0.1.0'.

The top-level semver.intersects(a, b, options) must give the same answers and must honor everything in options, including includePrerelease. This applies when a and b are strings and when they are Comparator objects, in both orders, with loose false and with loose true. For example, semver.intersects('<0.0.0', '<0.1.0', { loose: true }) and semver.intersects(new Comparator('<0.1.0'), new Comparator('<0.0.0-0'), { includePrerelease: true }) must both be false.

All other comparator and range intersection results must stay the same. Everything else must keep working.
